proposals.before: Half-moon chimes hung in the courtyard, qin and se on the dais, the eight instrument families alternating in concert—court music and ya ensemble together, antiphonal song above and wind below—each with its prescribed lyrics: the Zhou legacy.
proposals.after: Bells and chimes hung on all four sides in the courtyard, qin and se on the dais, the eight instrument families alternating in concert—court music and ya ensemble together, antiphonal song above and wind below—each with its prescribed lyrics: the Zhou legacy.
proposals.reason: 宮懸 is the palace arrangement of suspended bells and chimes on four sides; 'half-moon chimes' misstates the instruments' arrangement.

proposals.before: He held the heartland east of Shen; his fame knows no end.
proposals.after: He embraced the lands of the Shen field; his fame knows no end.
proposals.reason: 參墟 is the territory under the Shen lunar lodge (the old Jin land); 'east of Shen' adds an invented direction.

proposals.before: Filial and wise from youth, his fine renown long lay hidden.
proposals.after: Xiaozong, wise from youth, his fine renown long lay hidden.
proposals.reason: 孝宗 is Emperor Mu's temple name (Xiaozong), the subject of the line, not the adjective 'filial'.

proposals.before: He matched King Wen's pattern—silent, humble harmony.
proposals.after: He matched the pattern of his cultured late father—silent, humble harmony.
proposals.reason: 文考 means 'cultured late father' (Emperor Jianwen, Xiaowu's father), not King Wen of Zhou.

proposals.before: 《Ascending to the Turn》 became 《Wulin》, when Cao Cao swept downriver after taking Jingzhou and Zhou Yu met him at Wulin and drove him back.
proposals.after: 《Ascending to the Turn》 became 《Wulin》, when Cao Cao swept downriver after taking Jingzhou and Sun Quan ordered Zhou Yu to meet him at Wulin and drove him back.
proposals.reason: 權命將周瑜逆擊之: the idiomatic omits that Sun Quan ordered Zhou Yu to strike.

proposals.before: They changed 《Yellow Sparrow March》 to 《Boy Yi》, referring to how the red crow bore writing—Zhou rose thereby—and now the sage emperor received the mandate and spirit magpies came.
proposals.after: They changed 《Yellow Sparrow March》 to 《Bo Yi》, referring to how the red crow bore writing—Zhou rose thereby—and now the sage emperor received the mandate and spirit magpies came.
proposals.reason: 伯益 is the legendary minister Bo Yi; 'Boy Yi' is a mistranslation of the name.

proposals.before: Like punishing You-Hu, he smashes the five norms.
proposals.after: Like You-Hu of old, he threw the five norms into disorder.
proposals.reason: 追有扈，亂五常 describes the rebel Meng Da emulating You-Hu in disordering the five constants, not Xuan punishing You-Hu.

proposals.before: Abditions matched heaven's chronology; sage passed sage.
proposals.after: Abdications matched heaven's chronology; sage passed sage.
proposals.reason: 禪讓 means abdication; 'Abditions' is a misspelling that obscures the word.

proposals.before: Boy Yi helped Shun and Yu and ruled hill and stream.
proposals.after: Bo Yi helped Shun and Yu and ruled hill and stream.
proposals.reason: 伯益 is the legendary minister Bo Yi; 'Boy Yi' mistranslates the name.

proposals.before: Boy Yi aided Shun and Yu--office grasping mountains and rivers.
proposals.after: Bo Yi aided Shun and Yu--office grasping mountains and rivers.
proposals.reason: 伯益 is the legendary minister Bo Yi; 'Boy Yi' mistranslates the name.

proposals.before: In ages past at Tang and Yao court--sometimes seen amid cyan clouds.
proposals.after: In ages past at the court of Tang and Yu--sometimes seen amid cyan clouds.
proposals.reason: 唐虞 is Tang (Yao) and Yu (Shun); the literal wrongly gives 'Tang and Yao'.

proposals.before: Emperor Wen launched the great enterprise; prime virtue settled in Taishi.
proposals.after: Emperors Xuan and Wen launched the great enterprise; prime virtue settled in Taishi.
proposals.reason: 宣文 names both Emperor Xuan and Emperor Wen; the idiomatic drops Xuan.

proposals.before: Five emperors followed three kings; three kings were ages men admired.
proposals.after: Five Thearchs followed the Three Sovereigns; the Three Sovereigns were ages men admired.
proposals.reason: 三皇 are the Three Sovereigns, not 'three kings'.

proposals.before: Entrusted to align the seven powers, Cao Shuang once more drowned heaven.
proposals.after: Entrusted with the late ruler's charge, he aligned the seven powers; then Cao Shuang overreached heaven.
proposals.reason: 受遺齊七政 refers to Xuan receiving the testamentary charge; the idiomatic makes Cao Shuang the one entrusted.

proposals.before: August Great Jin; solemn blesses King Wen.
proposals.after: August Great Jin; solemn indeed is King Wen.
proposals.reason: 于穆文王 is 'Oh, solemn is King Wen'; 'solemn blesses' is ungrammatical.

proposals.before: Zhang Qian brought its method west but brought back only the 《Mahā-dūra》 tune.
proposals.after: Zhang Qian entered the Western Regions and brought its method to the Western Capital, but obtained only the 《Mahā-dūra》 tune.
proposals.reason: 張博望入西域，傳其法於西京: he went into the Western Regions and transmitted the method to the Western Capital; 'brought its method west' reverses the direction.

proposals.before: Later Han gave them to frontier commanders; under Emperor He only hosts above ten thousand might play them.
proposals.after: Later Han gave them to frontier commanders; under Emperor He generals commanding ten thousand men were permitted to use them.
proposals.reason: 萬人將軍得用之: generals of ten thousand men could use them; 'hosts above ten thousand might play them' misreads the rank.

proposals.before: In Xianhe 7 Cai Mo memorialized: "For the eighth-year Great Audience protocol, only wind-and-drum and bells should be performed; all other entertainments should be omitted."
proposals.after: In the seventh year of Xiankang under Emperor Cheng, Cai Mo memorialized: "For the eighth-year Great Audience protocol, only wind-and-drum and bells should be performed; all other entertainments should be omitted."
proposals.reason: 成帝咸康七年 is Xiankang 7 of Emperor Cheng, not Xianhe 7; the idiomatic also omits Emperor Cheng.

proposals.before: Wang Min loved his sister-in-law's maid; she sang while he flourished a white fan—hence the 《Round Fan》 ballad.
proposals.after: Secretariat Director Wang Min loved his sister-in-law's maid, whom the sister-in-law beat cruelly; the maid sang well and Wang Min liked to hold a white round fan—hence the 《Round Fan》 ballad.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic omits the sister-in-law's harsh beating of the maid and Wang Min's office, both stated in the Chinese.

proposals.before: Emperor Cheng Xianhe seventh year Minister Cai Mo memorialized: "Eighth year Great Audience protocol--only perform wind-drums bells--remaining skill music entirely not perform."
proposals.after: In Emperor Cheng’s seventh Xiankang year, Minister Cai Mo memorialized: “For the eighth-year Great Audience protocol, perform only wind-and-drum bells; omit all remaining entertainments.”
proposals.reason: 咸康 is Xiankang, not Xianhe; the sealed literal also drops 尚書 and misrenders the reign name. Align with the Chinese (and the already proposed idiomatic repair).

decisions.reason: The Chinese 宮懸 names bells and chimes suspended on four sides of the courtyard, not half-moon chimes.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 宮懸在庭，琴瑟在堂，八音迭奏，雅樂並作，登歌下管，各有常詠，周人之舊也。

decisions.reason: 奄有參墟 names holding the Shen-lodge territory; it does not state a direction east of Shen.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 奄有參墟，聲流無窮。

decisions.reason: 孝宗 is Emperor Mu’s temple name in this hymn line, not the adjective “filial.”

sourceWitness.excerpt: 孝宗夙哲，休音久臧。

decisions.reason: 文考 is his cultured deceased father (Emperor Jianwen), not King Wen of Zhou.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 同規文考，玄默允恭。

decisions.reason: 權命將周瑜逆擊之 states that Sun Quan ordered Zhou Yu to strike; the current idiomatic omits 權命.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 改《上之回》為《烏林》，言魏武既破荊州，順流東下，欲來爭鋒，權命將周瑜逆擊之于烏林而破走也。

decisions.reason: 伯益 is the minister Bo Yi; “Boy Yi” is not an acceptable rendering of the name.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 改《黃爵行》為《伯益》，言赤烏銜書，有周以興，今聖皇受命，神雀來也。

decisions.reason: 追有扈，亂五常 describes Meng Da’s disordering conduct; treatise gloss at s0166 ties the hymn to punishing Meng Da’s treason.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 追有扈，亂五常。

decisions.reason: 禪讓 is abdication; “Abditions” is a spelling error that blocks comprehension.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 禪讓應大曆，睿聖世相承。

decisions.reason: 伯益 is the minister Bo Yi; “Boy Yi” is not an acceptable rendering of the name.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 伯益佐舜禹，職掌山與川。

decisions.reason: 伯益 is the minister Bo Yi; “Boy Yi” is not an acceptable rendering of the name.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 伯益佐舜禹，職掌山與川。

decisions.reason: 唐虞 pairs Yao’s Tang and Shun’s Yu; the literal must not read Yao twice.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 昔在唐虞朝，時見青雲際。

decisions.reason: 宣文 names both Emperors Xuan and Wen; both must appear.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 宣文創洪業，盛德在泰始。

decisions.reason: 三皇 are the Three Sovereigns, not three kings.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 五帝繼三皇，三皇世所歸。

decisions.reason: 受遺齊七政 is Emperor Xuan’s testamentary charge in the Xuan hymn; 曹爽又滔天 is the parallel clause naming Cao Shuang.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 受遺齊七政，曹爽又滔天。

decisions.reason: 于穆文王 is an exclamatory Shijing-style line; “solemn blesses” is ungrammatical English.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 赫赫大晉，于穆文王。

decisions.reason: 張博望入西域，傳其法於西京 moves the method into the Western Capital; it is not “westward.”

sourceWitness.excerpt: 張博望入西域，傳其法於西京，惟得《摩訶兜勒》一曲。

decisions.reason: 萬人將軍得用之 names generals commanding ten thousand troops, not hosts who merely play music.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 後漢以給邊將，和帝時，萬人將軍得用之。

decisions.reason: 成帝咸康七年 is Emperor Cheng’s seventh Xiankang year, not Xianhe.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 成帝咸康七年，尚書蔡謨奏：「八年正會儀注，惟作鼓吹鐘鼓，其餘伎樂盡不作。」

decisions.reason: The Chinese gives Wang Min’s secretariat post, the sister-in-law’s beating, and the white round fan.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 《團扇歌》者，中書令王瑉與嫂婢有情，愛好甚篤，嫂捶撻婢過苦，婢素善歌，而瑉好捉白團扇，故制此歌。

decisions.reason: The literal must render 咸康 and 尚書 and align with the corrected idiomatic date.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 成帝咸康七年，尚書蔡謨奏：「八年正會儀注，惟作鼓吹鐘鼓，其餘伎樂盡不作。」
